title: A two-colouring of edges with both colours at every vertex of degree ≥ 2
statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph that is not an odd cycle (that is, $G$ is not a single cycle of odd length using every edge of $G$). Then the edges of $G$ can be assigned two colours in such a way that at every vertex $v$ of degree at least $2$, both colours are represented at $v$ — each of the two colours appears on some edge incident with $v$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is not an odd cycle (no odd-length cycle uses exactly all edges of $G$)
replaced:
Let $G$ be a connected graph that is not an odd cycle. Then $G$ has a 2-edge colouring
in which both colours are represented at each vertex of degree at least two.
